newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE FOREIGN BANKS MIXED ON MERGING FEARS.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE FOREIGN BANKS MIXED ON MERGING FEARS.

text.p: Singapore foreign bank shares stumbled in early Monday trade as fears of a possible merger of local and foreign tranches continued to haunt the market.
DBS Bank's foreign tranche surrendered early gains of 10 cents, dropping 20 cents to Singapore $17.20.
OCBC foreign also eased off its high of S$14.10, to S$13.70, down 10 cents within the first hour of trade.
"Some foreign banks were moving up this morning but those holding foreign shares are very, very worried," a remisier said.
UOB and OUB foreign, however, retained their gains but volumes were relatively sparse.
At 0200 GMT, the Straits Times Industrials Index was down 4.10 points to 1,939.82.
The index reversed after an initial blip to 1,948.58 on the back of an improved forecast for the economy, dealers said.
The economy was expanding faster than expected and would grow at six to seven percent in 1997, up from a revised five to seven percent, Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong said on Friday.
"Theoretically, the revision should help but the FOMC meeting and merging of dual listings has caused sentiment to be a bit cautious," said Violet Soh, research manager with Fraser Securities.
The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting on August 19 might usher in the long-anticipated rise in U.S. interest rates.
Actives were led by newly-listed Hotung, which rose to a debut high of US$0.54 against its initial public offer price of US$0.26.
The issue later fell back to US$0.49 on volume of 40 million shares.
